orbits.name: Very Low
orbits.description: Skimming the top of the atmosphere. Cheapest orbit to reach.
cons: Cannot meet a 30-day goal without help
orbits.source: Inspired by real early-1960s low parking orbits (e.g. Mercury-class, ~160-260 km).

orbits.name: Low
orbits.description: A good balance of cost and lifetime.
pros: Good balance of delta-v and lifetime
orbits.source: Inspired by real low Earth orbits used by early satellites and later crewed stations.

orbits.name: Medium-Low
orbits.description: High enough that drag is almost negligible.
orbits.source: Inspired by real early science satellites such as Explorer-class orbits, 1958-60s.

orbits.name: Polar
orbits.description: Passes over both poles, so it eventually sees the whole planet.
cons: Launch from the Cape needs a dogleg or another site
orbits.source: Inspired by real early polar-orbit satellites such as Discoverer / TIROS-class, 1959-60s.

orbits.name: High Elliptical
orbits.description: Lingers for hours over one region near apogee.
pros: Long communication windows over one region
cons: Passes through the Van Allen radiation belts
orbits.source: Inspired by real highly elliptical orbits such as Molniya (1965) and Explorer 6 (1959).

lifetime_table.notes: Simple lookup for the lifetime model: interpolate by altitude, then scale by ballistic coefficient (mass / (Cd * area)) relative to 1.0.
